findings.location: Evidence — Result bullet (line 33); propagated into Interpretation line 40
findings.evidence: Doc: "14 load-bearing claims — 9 verified / 0 refuted / 3 narrowed / 2 unverifiable → batch signal NO-GO." The cited gate record (docs/psv-gate-dogfood.gate-record.json) contradicts this: its own per-claim array G1–G14 yields 8 verified (G2,G3,G6,G9,G10,G11,G12,G14), 4 narrowed (G1,G7,G8,G13), 2 unverifiable (G4,G5) — the record's counts field ("verified": 9, "narrowed": 3) itself disagrees with its claims array (machine-recounted: {'narrowed': 4, 'verified': 8, 'unverifiable': 2}, total 14). The doc's narrative also names only G7/G8/G13 as narrowed, silently dropping G1 ('STORM abstract supports two-stage + pre-writing; 'cited article' attribute not in fetched text' — a narrowed verdict in the record). The doc reproduces the record's wrong counts field instead of its adjudication data.

findings.location: Proposed design — Gate bullet (line 23) vs Risks R3 (line 70)
findings.evidence: Doc line 23 (explicit rule PSVGM-02): "NO-GO iff any load-bearing claim is refuted OR unverifiable, OR ≥2 load-bearing claims are narrowed; GO otherwise." Doc line 70 (R3 mitigation): "a single refuted claim does not NO-GO (threshold in ODP-5)." For one refuted LOAD-BEARING claim the rule says NO-GO while R3 says not-NO-GO — the two statements conflict as written, with no load-bearing/non-load-bearing qualifier in R3. Additionally R3's parenthetical mis-points: "threshold in ODP-5" references ODP-5, whose actual subject is "cost threshold: write a quantified q·C > p gate rule into the guide vs keep the qualitative rule-13 conditions" (line 64) — a cost threshold, not the batch-verdict threshold the rule already fixes. The batch threshold for refuted non-load-bearing claims is also left undefined.
findings.suggestion: Qualify R3 to "a single refuted NON-load-bearing claim does not NO-GO" and repoint the parenthetical (or delete it — the threshold is fixed by the gate rule).

findings.evidence: Doc line 40: "q > 0 on this sample; gate cost ≈ 1.5 rounds vs 5 csr rounds saved on a NO-GO doc → q·C > p holds here." Doc line 64: "write a quantified q·C > p gate rule into the guide." The symbols q, C, p are never defined anywhere in the doc, and a repo-wide search finds no definition (only round1-same.json PSVGM-06's bare use of 'q>0'/"q≈0"). The doc's central cost-benefit conclusion and ODP-5's entire proposal depend on this notation; a reader cannot evaluate "q·C > p" (which quantity is q — gate catch-rate? and what are C and p?) without the external 2026-08-09 discussion the doc never glosses (workspace rule 10).
findings.suggestion: Define q, C, p inline at first use (e.g., q = P(gate catches a defect csr's recall misses), C = csr round cost, p = gate cost).

findings.evidence: Doc: "the two q≈0 samples are THEMSELVES rule-13-qualifying (the fix-plan doc ran the rule-13 chain) — the rule-13 trigger alone does NOT separate them from the q>0 sample... the q≈0 samples cited almost exclusively local files." Only ONE sample is identified (the fix-plan doc, whose psv record docs/record-auditability-fix-plan.psv-record.json indeed adjudicates "All adjudication sources local... no network fetch"). The second q≈0 sample is never named, and no other psv record exists in docs/ or workspace/ to identify it. The counter-evidence argument cannot be audited without that referent.
findings.suggestion: Name the second q≈0 sample (and cite its record), or restate as "the fix-plan q≈0 sample"

findings.evidence: Doc: "gate cost ≈ 1.5 rounds vs 5 csr rounds saved on a NO-GO doc → q·C > p holds here." The "5 csr rounds saved" figure's only source is the gate record's own cost_ledger assertion ("would have saved 5 csr rounds on a citation-broken doc") — the record states it with no basis, and I could not verify any repo artifact grounding it (the fix-plan csr-run shows cap=5 for a different doc, which is a cap, not a saved-rounds count; memory notes long-doc csr runs take up to 7 rounds). The doc promotes this unsourced figure into its quantitative q·C > p conclusion. This is the honest-disclosure item: the q·C > p claim is not independently checkable.
findings.suggestion: Ground the saved-rounds figure (e.g., in a real csr run on the same artifact) or downgrade the claim to "likely saves ≥1 csr round" until ODP-5 quantifies it.

findings.evidence: Doc line 71: "R4 — evidence experiment selects an unrepresentative doc. (The subject is real and non-synthetic, so only the "own artifact" half of the criterion is in question — but as written the doc's own mitigation was not honored by its executed evidence.)

findings.location: Evidence section, line 41 (definitions adv-3) vs lines 40/42 + gate-record cost_ledger
findings.evidence: Proposal defines: "**q** = P(the gate catches a defect csr's recall-level verification would miss, on this doc class); **C** = csr round cost; **p** = gate cost. The decision rule is q·C > p (gate worth it when expected saved csr cost exceeds gate cost)". With the doc's own numbers — p ≈ 222k tokens (line 40; gate-record `total_tokens_approx: 222251`), C = "~100-140k tokens each" (gate-record `comparable_csr_rounds`), i.e. p ≈ 1.5C — the rule requires q > p/C ≈ 1.5, which no probability q ∈ [0,1] satisfies. The rule as parameterized can never fire, yet the doc presents it as the decision rule and ODP-5 proposes to "write a quantified q·C > p gate rule into the guide". The verbal gloss "expected saved csr cost" implies C is the multi-round saved run (line 42: "the gate saves the csr investment — ≥1 round, bounded above by the long-doc cap (5–7)"), contradicting the definition "C = csr round cost". Either the definition or the gloss is wrong; as written the rule is vacuous.
findings.suggestion: Define C as the expected saved csr investment (multi-round, 1..cap) or restate the rule with per-round cost; make the unit explicit.

findings.location: Proposed design, line 23 (N10) + Evidence line 39 (G15–G21, PSVGM-01) + gate-record escalated array
findings.evidence: Proposal line 39: "G15–G21 (gate-external escalations — NOT counted in M=14; unfetched, non-extracted): the doc's largest borrowable decision (EverOS) rests on a user-supplied X-post with NO URL in the artifact — unfetchable ... (These are gate-external, distinct from psv's K semantics, which counts only EXTRACTED claims — PSVGM-01.)" The cited authority says the opposite: psv SKILL.md step 2 — "A claim whose only adjudicating source is volatile ... is still admissible, but mark it volatile at extraction so the registry in the coverage-record captures it" — unfetchable-source claims ARE extracted, counted, and marked. Meanwhile the doc's own N10 (line 23) defines the gate's extraction surface as load-bearing claims ("the gate NEVER extracts non-load-bearing claims") and its own line 39 calls EverOS "the doc's largest borrowable decision" / "an adoption-load-bearing source" — so the gate excluded its single largest in-scope load-bearing claim from M via a rationale ("K counts only EXTRACTED claims") that is true-but-irrelevant, since G15–G21 were enumerated with claim IDs and substantive notes in the record. Additionally the batch rule (PSVGM-02) has no vocabulary for gate-external escalations — how a 'flagged' unfetchable load-bearing claim interacts with GO/NO-GO is undefined, so a GO signal can ignore the doc's largest load-bearing risk.
findings.suggestion: Either count unfetchable load-bearing claims as unverifiable (K) per SKILL.md step 2, or define explicitly in PSVGM-02 how gate-external escalations participate in the batch signal.

findings.location: Evidence lines 34 + 42 vs Proposed design line 23 (UNVERIFIABLE action), against psv SKILL.md taxonomy
findings.evidence: Line 34: "G5 (LOAD-BEARING, unverifiable): the doc's SAG rejection premise ... is NOT in the fetched SAG abstract — 'incremental writes' ≠ 'append-only'. The adoption decision's cited property is unsupported by the oracle." Line 42: "the gate caught citation-quality defects (an unsupported load-bearing premise + a misattribution)" — the q>0 evidence rests on G5 as a caught defect. But line 23 defines the unverifiable action as: "UNVERIFIABLE load-bearing → VERIFIER-side re-fetch first (full-text fetch may resolve it, as G4/G5's abstract-limited status suggests), and only rework if the re-fetch confirms the gap" — i.e., the gap is UNCONFIRMED pending re-fetch. And psv SKILL.md step 3 defines unverifiable as "no fetchable source adjudicates it" — not a defect finding; SKILL.md line 14: a finding that cannot ground a fetched quote is "downgraded to unverifiable, never asserted". The doc asserts the premise as an unsupported defect (line 34/42) while its own action semantics say the gap is not confirmed. An unverifiable is counted as q>0 evidence in the interpretation while the same doc's NO-GO action treats it as unresolved.
findings.suggestion: State in the interpretation that the q>0 evidence rests on the 4 narrowed claims (G1/G7/G8/G13) and the unverifiable G5 is pending re-fetch — not a confirmed catch.

findings.location: Evidence line 43 (counter-evidence sample (2)) vs line 41 (q definition), against fix-plan psv-record coverage line 16
findings.evidence: Line 41 defines q as "P(the gate catches a defect csr's recall-level verification would miss, on this doc class)" — no refuted-only restriction. Line 43 labels the fix-plan run q≈0: "the q≈0 label rests on: 0 refuted + narrowed claims locally adjudicated (N04)". But the fix-plan psv-record (docs/record-auditability-fix-plan.psv-record.json) coverage line 16 records "4 narrowed (P8 field enumeration; P13 'only' overstatement; P37 §2.5-vs-§3 enumeration; P73 escalate-target not named in SKILL.md) — all addressed in the doc" — on an artifact the record itself marks "(csr-converged)": real post-csr defect catches by psv, exactly the q-definition event. The positive sample (dogfood) has 0 refuted too and is labeled q>0 on narrowed+unverifiable evidence. The q labels are assigned by refuted-count for the negative samples and by catch-class for the positive one — the same evidence class (narrowed catches) is counted as q for the dogfood and excluded from q for the fix-plan sample, without citing the fix-plan csr-run record to establish those 4 were csr-caught first.
findings.suggestion: Either show from the fix-plan csr-run record that P8/P13/P37/P73 were already csr findings, or relabel the fix-plan sample per the same catch-class standard applied to the dogfood.

findings.location: Status/scope line 4 + Boundary line 57 vs Proposed design line 23 (re-verify loop)
findings.evidence: Line 4: "the gate is the same pipeline FAMILY run twice (subset then full), not a loop" and line 57: "psv ADR #1 (single pipeline, NOT a debate loop) — the gate is the same pipeline run twice, not a loop." Line 23: "Re-verify loop: after rework/re-fetch, the affected claims are RE-RUN through the gate (cheap subset pass) before any csr investment — a re-gate is required to re-establish GO." On the rework path the pipeline runs ≥3 times (gate → rework → re-gate → csr → full psv) and the design has iterate-until-GO semantics — yet the doc's central scoping claim is "run twice, not a loop". The boundary between the allowed re-gate iteration and the ADR #1-forbidden "debate loop / cap / stalemate" (ADR #1 decision text) is never defined — a load-bearing distinction for the doc's own ADR #1-non-violation claim. psv has no existing cap/stalemate machinery for re-gate iteration either; how many re-gates before abandon is unspecified.
findings.suggestion: Define the loop/re-run boundary explicitly and specify re-gate iteration bounds (or a cap) so the 'not a loop / ADR #1 intact' claim is checkable.

findings.evidence: Proposal: "The GATE has its own M=0 semantics (PSVGM-07): under a locked rule-13 trigger, gate-M=0 signals TRIGGER-MISAPPLICATION (the doc does not qualify after all — a qualifying doc has load-bearing claims by definition), escalated with its own wording". The authoritative source the gate inherits from names a second cause for M=0: psv SKILL.md line 26 — "claim extraction inherits the extractor's blind spots — claims neither author nor extractor can see are absent from M". A gate extraction on a truly rule-13-qualifying doc can yield subset-M=0 because the extractor missed the load-bearing claims — the signal semantics assert trigger-misapplication as the meaning, silently excluding a documented alternative cause. The doc's own rule 3 (never silently green; state coverage gaps honestly) is the standard this over-assertion fails.
findings.suggestion: Add extractor-blind-spot as an equally possible cause in PSVGM-07's signal semantics (e.g. 'trigger-misapplication OR extractor miss — human adjudicates').

findings.evidence: The doc applies a re-fetchability standard to its counter-evidence — line 43: "the 0-refuted half is not independently re-fetchable" (used as the volatility-defect evidence) — but its own positive evidence fails that same standard: the gate-record's 14 per-claim entries carry verdict + note only, with NO source_refs, NO fetched quotes, and NO URLs (contrast the fix-B doc-findings packet contract: claim_ref / verdict / source_ref / fetched quote, SKILL.md step 4), and the fetched texts (SAG abstract, STORM abstract, Anthropic article, agent-teams doc) are not persisted anywhere. The proposal's q>0 evidence (G5 premise 'unsupported', G7 'adversarial' 0 times, G8 80% BrowseComp, G13 worktree, G1 'cited article') is therefore not independently re-fetchable — the identical defect class the doc flags in the q≈0 samples and in fix B — and the doc does not disclose this asymmetry. Something required for soundness is absent: re-fetchable grounding for the evidence that carries the proposal's q>0 claim.
findings.suggestion: Disclose in the evidence section that gate verdicts are not independently re-fetchable (no persisted fetched quotes/source refs) — same standard applied to the counter-evidence — or persist the fetched quotes as the psv fix-B contract requires.
